newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says no need for couterweight to ECB.
newsitem.headline: Germany says no need for couterweight to ECB.

text.p: The German finance ministry, responding to statements from opposition leader Oskar Lafontaine, on Thursday said there was no need for an economic council alongside the European Central Bank in monetary union.
"There is no need for a counterweight to the European Central Bank," a ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.
On Thursday Lafontaine said he supported France's demand to create a 'European economic government' as a counterweight to Europe's planned independent central bank.
"Politicians can make mistakes -- but so can institutions which are apparently independent," he said in Saarbruecken, capital of the Saar state where he is premier.
But the finance ministry spokeswoman said after the start of monetary union responsibilities for finance, economic and budget policies would remain in the hands of state governments.

There were sufficient means provided by the Maastricht treaty on economic and monetary union (EMU) for European Union member states to establish the necessary procedures to coordinate such policies, she added.
"Monetary stability must not become a matter of politics," she said.
